This page runs a deterministic analysis on ten feet of a driving record
typed in by hand. The [walkthrough](../examples/walkthrough.qmd) does the same
on a full benchmark log and explains each stage.

## Inputs

A driving record is the inspector's log: for each foot the pile advanced,
the hammer speed in blows per minute and the number of blows it took.
The package also needs the pile, the hammer and a description of the
ground.

::: {#1ea2d95f .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import driven_pile as dp

bpm = np.array([55, 55, 53, 48, 42, 42, 50, 50, 49, 46])
bpf = np.array([3, 5, 5, 7, 4, 9, 13, 20, 22, 20])

pile = dp.Pile.octagonal(width_in=24, length_ft=60)
hammer = dp.Hammer(ram_weight=20.0)  # kips

log = dp.DriveLog.from_arrays(
    pile,
    hammer,
    bpm=bpm,
    bpf=bpf,
    depth=np.arange(1, 11),  # ft below the first logged foot
    tip_elevation=-50.0,     # ft, toe elevation at the end of the drive
)
```
:::


The stroke, which the capacity formula needs, is derived from the blow rate
by free-fall timing.

::: {#fd7f6847 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6, 4), sharey=True)
ax1.plot(log.bpf, log.elevation, "o-")
ax1.set_xlabel("blows per foot")
ax1.set_ylabel("elevation (ft)")
ax2.plot(log.stroke, log.elevation, "o-")
ax2.set_xlabel("stroke (ft)")
for a in (ax1, ax2):
    a.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![The driving record. Blows per foot as logged, and the stroke derived from the blow rate.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=522 height=357}
:::
:::


The soil profile gives the mudline, the water table and the fines content.
A single fines value makes a uniform profile; a table of elevation versus
percent fines is interpolated.

::: {#f06727cc .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
soil = dp.SoilProfile(mudline=-10.0, water_elevation=-10.0, fines=15.0)
```
:::


Here the first logged foot is 31 ft below the mudline, so the pile passed
through 30 ft of soil that the log says nothing about. The method treats
that unlogged top segment separately, as the next steps show.

## The three stages

`prepare_target` turns the log into a capacity target: the recalibrated
Danish formula applied to each foot, smoothed, and placed on a one-foot
grid that runs from the mudline to the toe.

::: {#d6389e8f .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
target = dp.prepare_target(log, soil)
```
:::


::: {#4a3110bf .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 5))
ax.plot(target.raw_capacity, target.elevation, ".", color="gray", label="formula per foot")
ax.plot(target.capacity, target.elevation, color="C0", label="smoothed target")
ax.axhline(target.mudline, color="k", lw=0.8, ls="--")
ax.set_xlabel("capacity at time of driving (kips)")
ax.set_ylabel("elevation (ft)")
ax.legend(loc="lower left")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Formula capacity per foot (points) and the smoothed target (line). The dashed line is the mudline; the grid above the first logged foot has no target.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){width=411 height=431}
:::
:::


`sweep_top_phi` tries a constant friction angle for the top segment and
keeps the values whose fit to the log is as good as the best one. The
admissible band is the range of top-segment friction angles the log cannot
distinguish between.

::: {#a4616d99 .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
band = dp.sweep_top_phi(target)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5))
ax.plot(band.phi, band.rms, "o-")
ax.axvspan(band.lo, band.hi, color="C0", alpha=0.15)
ax.set_xlabel("top-segment friction angle (deg)")
ax.set_ylabel("RMS misfit (kips)")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Misfit of the march versus the assumed top-segment friction angle. The shaded range is the admissible band.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=445 height=320}
:::
:::


`run_drive` marches down the grid, characterizing each logged foot from the
toe resistance the target demands and tracking the pore pressure that
later blows generate. The deterministic analysis uses the lowest admissible
top-segment friction angle.

::: {#db07a7ed .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code}
result = dp.run_drive(target, top_phi=band.lo)
```
:::


## Results

::: {#a77df450 .cell execution_count=8}
``` {.python .cell-code}
result.plot_fit()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Capacity target and the modeled capacity at the time of driving.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-9-output-1.png){width=411 height=547}
:::
:::


::: {#8f164605 .cell execution_count=9}
``` {.python .cell-code}
result.plot_profile()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Friction angle, equivalent blow count and end-of-drive pore-pressure ratio. The dashed line is the top of the logged record.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-10-output-1.png){width=747 height=504}
:::
:::


The long-term capacity is the shaft resistance after the pore pressure has
dissipated plus the toe resistance at the end of the drive. No toe setup is
modeled.

::: {#b5961128 .cell execution_count=10}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print(f"end of drive {result.eod_capacity:.0f} kips")
print(f"long term    {result.ltc:.0f} kips "
      f"= shaft {result.ltc_shaft:.0f} + toe {result.toe_eod:.0f}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
end of drive 701 kips
long term    862 kips = shaft 266 + toe 595
```
:::
:::


Every foot carries an outcome code. `ok` means the toe resistance was
reconciled with a friction angle inside the bounds; `above_ceiling` and
`below_floor` mean it was pinned at a bound.

::: {#fa6dc9f3 .cell execution_count=11}
``` {.python .cell-code}
result.reason_counts()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11}
```
{'ok': 10}
```
:::
:::


## One call

`analyze` runs the same three stages and returns them together, with the
Monte Carlo simulation available on request.

```python
out = dp.analyze(log, soil)            # out.drive, out.top_band
out = dp.analyze(log, soil, run_mc=True)  # adds out.mc
```
